named_subject: a crab (dome-shaped shell with a large claw hanging at lower left, a smaller claw at the right, and short legs underneath)
action: The crab stands almost still; the lower-left claw changes shape and shifts slightly around frames 7-8 and then returns to its earlier pose, with no other visible movement.
identity_gap: The doodle has both claws raised high above the body on long arms with four legs below, while the animation has one claw hanging below the body, the other folded at the side, and an arm stroke cutting straight down through the shell, so it reads as a different drawing built from the same parts.
notes: The film is a nearly still ghost crab whose clear event is the eyestalks folding down and coming back up in frames 8-11, and the animation shows no eyes and no matching event; its only change is a claw that pops in frames 7-8 and snaps back at 9. The change that would help most is keeping the doodle's raised-claw layout and putting the film's motion into eyestalks drawn on top of the shell (fold down over frames 8-10, rise in 11) instead of changing the claw.
